societies.name: Third Imperium
societies.subtitle: The dominant human polity in Charted Space
societies.description: Eleven thousand worlds spanning dozens of sectors. Citizens of the Third Imperium grow up navigating Imperial law, bureaucracy, and a cosmopolitan culture shaped by centuries of trade. Characters from here have the widest range of species options — humans, Vargr, Aslan, and a dozen other sophonts all hold Imperial citizenship.

societies.name: Solomani Confederation
societies.subtitle: Children of Terra — humanity's original homeworld
societies.description: The Solomani Confederation claims dominion over the region of space closest to Earth, the original human homeworld. Solomani culture prizes human heritage, individual initiative, and a fierce pride in their claim to be the 'true' humans. Relations with the Third Imperium are often tense, sometimes outright hostile.

societies.name: Aslan Hierate / Glorious Empire
societies.subtitle: Honor, clan, and the eternal drive for land
societies.description: The Aslan Hierate is one of the great powers of Charted Space — a confederation of powerful clans driven by an ancient code of honor, a biological imperative toward land ownership, and strict gender-defined social roles. The Glorious Empire is a rival Aslan state in the Trojan Reach — brutal, expansionist, and locked in permanent conflict with the Hierate. Both share Aslan biology and the Rite of Passage, but their cultures and careers differ sharply. Imperial humans who find themselves in Glorious Empire space are enslaved — they may only take the Slave career.

societies.name: Hiver Federation
societies.subtitle: Masters of manipulation, architects of stability
societies.description: The Hivers are six-limbed starfish-shaped beings who never communicate directly — all Hiver interaction is through elaborate indirect manipulation. Their Federation is ancient, stable, and remarkably successful. A handful of humans live and work within Federation space. Hiver Travellers use Resolve (RES) in place of Social Standing and advance via the status table (Adult → Senior → Manipulator) rather than conventional ranks.

societies.name: Droyne Oytrip
societies.subtitle: Caste-bound community of an ancient alien species
societies.description: The Droyne are an ancient species organised entirely around caste. At adolescence (age 12) each Droyne undergoes the Iskyar ritual, drawing golden coyns to determine which of six castes they belong to for life: Worker, Warrior, Drone, Technician, Sport, or Leader. Droyne have no Social Standing — their position is defined by caste and how highly their Oytrip values them. They roll 1D+1 for most characteristics (not 2D) and always have PSI. No mishap automatically ejects a Droyne — instead they make a continuation check each time misfortune strikes.

societies.name: Zhodani Consulate
societies.subtitle: A psionic meritocracy beyond the Spinward frontier
societies.description: The Zhodani are humans who embraced psionics thousands of years ago and built their entire society around it. Consulate citizens are routinely tested for psionic potential; those who possess it rise in status. The Consulate is orderly, egalitarian within its caste system, and regarded with deep suspicion by the Imperium.

societies.name: Two Thousand Worlds
societies.subtitle: The K'Kree herd-empire — and those who must live within it
societies.description: The Two Thousand Worlds is the vast interstellar empire of the K'Kree — six-limbed centauroid obligate herbivores who regard meat-eaters with deep revulsion. Humans who inhabit K'Kree space are rare, operate under strict dietary laws, and are considered of low status. Play as a K'Kree patriarch and track your family group across four castes: Pastoral, Servant, Merchant, and Noble.

societies.name: Vargr Extents
societies.subtitle: A thousand shifting pack-states beyond the Imperial border
societies.description: The Vargr Extents are not a unified polity — they are a region of space coreward of the Imperium populated by thousands of small Vargr states, alliances, and raider bands, constantly shifting as charisma rises and falls. Vargr raised here are shaped by pack loyalty, personal magnetism, and a fluid concept of authority.

societies.name: Other / Far Domains
societies.subtitle: Sword Worlds, Trojan Reach, Drinax, and beyond
societies.description: The frontiers of Charted Space are home to dozens of smaller human states, pocket empires, and isolated communities. The Sword Worlds are a confederation of worlds with a fierce Scandinavian-influenced culture. The Kingdom of Drinax, the Trojan Reach, Reft Sector, and other border regions produce hard, self-reliant people shaped by distance from any major power.
